events.title: Assassination of President John F. Kennedy
events.description: U.S. President John F. Kennedy was shot and killed while riding in a motorcade through Dealey Plaza in Dallas, Texas. Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested later that day, and Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson was sworn in as president aboard Air Force One.
events.significance: The assassination shocked the nation and the world, led to the Warren Commission investigation, and remains one of the most scrutinized and debated events in American history, shaping public trust in government and the era's political direction.

events.title: Margaret Thatcher Announces Resignation
events.description: After failing to secure a decisive win in the first round of a Conservative Party leadership challenge, Margaret Thatcher announced she would resign as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, ending more than eleven years in office.
events.significance: Her departure ended the era of the longest-serving British prime minister of the 20th century and reshaped the Conservative Party, with John Major succeeding her.

events.title: Lebanon Gains Independence from France
events.description: Lebanon's independence was recognized after a crisis in which French Mandate authorities arrested Lebanese leaders, including President Bechara El Khoury, prompting popular protests and international pressure that led to their release.
events.significance: The date is celebrated as Lebanese Independence Day and marked the end of French Mandate rule, establishing the foundations of the modern Lebanese state and its National Pact power-sharing arrangement.

events.title: Birth of Modern-Era Milestone: Release of Rockefeller-Era... (Correction: Mexico City hosts) — Actually: Death of Mae West
events.description: American actress, playwright, and screenwriter Mae West, famed for her witty double entendres and challenges to censorship, died in Los Angeles at age 87.
events.significance: West was a pioneering figure who pushed boundaries on gender and sexuality in Hollywood and left a lasting influence on American comedy and popular culture.

events.title: Death of Aldous Huxley and C. S. Lewis
events.description: On the same day President Kennedy was assassinated, British author Aldous Huxley, writer of 'Brave New World,' and C. S. Lewis, author of 'The Chronicles of Narnia,' both died.
events.significance: Both deaths were overshadowed by Kennedy's assassination, yet the two authors left enduring legacies in dystopian fiction, fantasy literature, and Christian apologetics.
